record.paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
record.original_question: What physical mechanisms launch highly ionized gas close to active galactic nuclei, and how are those ionized outflows connected to other feedback mechanisms such as jets or larger-scale outflows?

evidence.quote: Session 3 was devoted to different forms of feedback observed in low- and high-redshift AGN, such as jets and outflows.
Significant amounts of highly ionized gas seem to be launched closer to the AGN, however the physical mechanisms and possible connection between them are still matter of debate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the context of active galactic nuclei (AGN) — accreting supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies that drive multiphase feedback into their surroundings — observations show that substantial amounts of highly ionized gas are launched on small scales close to the central engine, in addition to relativistic jets and larger-scale (kpc-scale) ionized, neutral, and molecular outflows.

Identify and characterize the physical mechanisms responsible for launching the highly ionized gas component close to the AGN (for example, radiation-pressure driving on lines and dust, magnetohydrodynamic/magneto-centrifugal acceleration from an accretion disk, thermal driving from an X-ray-heated corona, or jet-induced acceleration), and determine quantitatively how this small-scale ionized outflow phase is causally and energetically connected to other AGN feedback channels such as relativistic jets and large-scale galactic outflows. In particular, establish under which AGN luminosity, accretion-rate, and host-galaxy conditions each launching mechanism dominates, and provide a unified description linking the nuclear ionized outflow to jet activity and to the kpc-scale multiphase outflows.
artifact.status_search_result: The mechanisms launching nuclear highly ionized outflows in AGN (e.g., ultra-fast outflows, warm absorbers) and their connection to jets and galaxy-scale outflows remain an active research topic; recent reviews continue to discuss radiation-driven, MHD, and thermally driven scenarios without a consensus, and the coupling between nuclear winds and large-scale multiphase outflows is still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: AGN feedback and its connection to nuclear winds (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews of AGN-driven outflows emphasize that the launching mechanisms of ultra-fast and highly ionized nuclear winds (radiation pressure, MHD, thermal) and their link to kpc-scale outflows are still debated.
status_evidence.claim: The driving mechanisms and the connection of nuclear ionized outflows to jets and galaxy-scale outflows remain open.
